title: Where do customers come from?
principle: Find one channel that works, and master it first.

screens.text: Let me tell you about Traction, a book on how new businesses find customers. Gabriel Weinberg and Justin Mares wrote it. They asked more than 40 founders how they found their first customers. Most people starting a business guess wrong about this.

screens.prompt: What do you think many of these founders did to find customers?

options.label: Tried different ways, then focused on one
Tried all ways at once, with equal effort
Spent most of their money on ads

screens.why: Many tried different ways to find customers. When one worked, they focused on it. In the book, investor Peter Thiel says one way is very likely to work best.

screens.title: The Bullseye framework
screens.text: A channel is a way customers find you, like WhatsApp groups, Instagram, a café counter or flyers. The book lists 19 channels. It teaches the Bullseye framework. First, list many ways. Then test a few without spending much. Finally, focus on the one that works.

screens.prompt: These are the Bullseye steps, but they are in the wrong order. Put the first step at the top.
steps: List all the channels you could use
Pick the three most likely to work
Test each one without spending much and count orders
Spend most of your time on the one that works
screens.why: Good. First, think of many ways. Then test a few without spending much. Finally, focus on the one that works. Let the test results guide you.

screens.title: Now look at your business
screens.text: Both a tech company and a home bakery need a way to find customers. It's early May. You bake cakes at home. Each ₹850 cake leaves you ₹450. You want 10 new families a month. So last month, you tested six ways.

screens.prompt: Here are your six test results. For each one, tell me: should you keep testing it or stop?

items.text: Posts in colony WhatsApp groups: free, 6 orders
Instagram videos, paid ₹1,000 to reach more people: 4 orders
Ad paper inside a newspaper: ₹3,000, no orders
A card kept on the café counter: free, 3 orders
A large ad board near the station: ₹5,000, 1 order

screens.why: Good. WhatsApp, Instagram and the café card brought orders for little or no money. The other ways cost ₹2,000 to ₹5,000 and brought just one order or none.

screens.prompt: WhatsApp groups brought 6 free orders. Instagram brought 4 for ₹1,000, and the café card brought 3. What will you do next month?

options.label: Give equal time to all three ways
Give most time to WhatsApp groups
Try three new ways to find customers

screens.why: Right. WhatsApp groups brought the most orders without costing money. Focus more on them. Try more colonies, use better photos and reply faster. Keep using the other two a little.

wrong.a: Giving equal time sounds fair. But WhatsApp groups brought the most free orders. So give them most of your time.
wrong.c: You have already found a way that works. You can try new ways later. For now, focus more on WhatsApp groups.

screens.prompt: Your posts work best in your own colony's WhatsApp group. Why should you first get more buyers there before trying the next colony?

options.label: Happy buyers may tell people in other colonies
Joining many groups may cost too much money
People in other colonies may not buy cakes

screens.why: Yes. Remember Unit 2: first get many buyers in one group. When people in your colony know and love your cakes, they tell people in the next colony.

wrong.b: Joining WhatsApp groups is free. Remember Unit 2: first get many buyers in one group. Happy buyers can then tell people in the next colony.
wrong.c: You don't know that. Remember Unit 2: first get many buyers in one group. Happy buyers can then tell people in the next colony.

screens.setup: It's mid-May. Most families in your colony now know you, and WhatsApp groups bring 8 new families a month. A sales agent offers to put your ad in newspapers going to 50,000 homes for ₹15,000. Each cake leaves you ₹450.
screens.question: How will you spend your time and money this month?

options.label: Buy the newspaper ad to reach more homes
options.outcome: The ad brings 3 orders. They leave you ₹1,350, but you spent ₹15,000. You also spend less time posting in WhatsApp groups. So those groups bring only 5 families this month.
options.why: Reaching 50,000 homes sounded good. But your earlier test showed that newspaper ads brought very few orders.
options.better: Focus more on WhatsApp. Join groups in the colonies next to yours.

options.label: Buy a smaller ad and keep using WhatsApp
options.outcome: A ₹5,000 newspaper ad brings 1 order. WhatsApp still brings 8 families, as before. You spent ₹5,000 on the ad and got ₹450 back.
options.why: You kept using your best channel. But you also spent money on a channel your earlier test showed did not work well.
options.better: Focus more on WhatsApp. Join groups in the colonies next to yours.

options.label: Join WhatsApp groups in two nearby colonies
options.outcome: People in your colony already tell neighbours in those colonies about your cakes. You share real photos and reply fast. This month, you get 13 new families instead of 8. That's ₹2,250 more profit, with no money spent.
options.why: You focused on a channel that already worked. You first built buyers in one colony, then reached the next.

screens.text: Test a few ___ without spending much. Then spend most of your time on the ___ that works.
screens.why: Exactly. That's the Bullseye framework. Your test showed that WhatsApp groups worked best. Reaching one more colony brought 13 families instead of 8.

summary: A channel is a way customers find you. One channel often works much better than the others.
The Bullseye framework: list many channels, test a few without spending much, then focus on the one that works.
Choose your channel using test results, not how many people it might reach.

cards.front: Flyers cost ₹2,000 and bring 1 order. WhatsApp is free and brings 6 orders. Where will you focus?
cards.back: Focus on the channel that works before trying more.

cards.front: What are the steps of the Bullseye framework?
options: List many, test a few, master one
cards.back: List many channels, test a few without spending much, then focus on the best one.

cards.front: An agent offers an ad reaching 50,000 homes. Your last test of this kind brought no orders. What will you do?
options: Say no and go deeper on what works
cards.back: Choose using your test results, not how many homes the ad could reach.

sources.label: Gabriel Weinberg and Justin Mares, Traction (Portfolio/Penguin, 2015): publisher's page
